title: HDHP vs. PPO Break-Even
description: Annual-cost comparator for an HDHP+HSA against a PPO: the break-even medical spend (first $50 grid point in [0, 20000] where the HDHP total is <= the PPO total), the two totals at the expected spend, the winner and savings, a fixed key-spend comparison table, the HSA tax shield, and a recommendation. Pure function of the declared input domain with an explicit as_of date; the node reads no clock. Port of ApexLogics #105 (AL-112). Port provenance: Apex page https://apexlogics.org/tools/105-hdhp-vs-ppo-break-even/ fetched 2026-10-13 (sha256 ba3010ef002501d03ffc95fcc0c75ca1038235c230554e2df067dec57649a460), tasking APEXPORT-105 (GRADES PASS-PENDING-XV 2026-10-14, Builder-verifies-at-land 12/12 vectors re-executed 2026-10-19), landed by APEX-PORT-105-LAND-1 on 2026-10-19.

as_of.description: Run date, a real calendar date as YYYY-MM-DD. The node never reads a clock; it echoes this value so the record is deterministic. (The Apex source stamps a wall-clock timestamp here; the port replaces it with this explicit input.)

coverage.description: HSA coverage class; selects the 2026 HSA contribution limit used to cap the tax shield (individual $4,400, family $8,750).

hdhp_premium_monthly.description: HDHP monthly premium in USD dollars; multiplied by 12 for the annual premium.

hdhp_deductible.description: HDHP annual deductible in USD dollars.

hdhp_oop_max.description: HDHP annual out-of-pocket maximum in USD dollars.

hdhp_coinsurance_pct.description: HDHP coinsurance rate as a percent in [0, 100] applied to spend above the deductible.

ppo_premium_monthly.description: PPO monthly premium in USD dollars; multiplied by 12 for the annual premium.

ppo_deductible.description: PPO annual deductible in USD dollars.

ppo_oop_max.description: PPO annual out-of-pocket maximum in USD dollars.

ppo_coinsurance_pct.description: PPO coinsurance rate as a percent in [0, 100] applied to spend above the deductible.

employer_hsa.description: Employer HSA contribution in USD dollars per year; added to additional_hsa, then capped at the coverage HSA limit for the shield.

additional_hsa.description: Additional personal HSA contribution in USD dollars per year; added to employer_hsa, then capped at the coverage HSA limit for the shield.

marginal_tax_rate_pct.description: Marginal tax rate (federal + state) as a percent in [0, 100]; the HSA tax shield is (capped contributions) times this rate.

expected_annual_spend.description: Expected annual medical spend in USD dollars; the point at which the two totals, the winner and the recommendation are evaluated.

mcp_tool_definition.name: estimate_hdhp_ppo_breakeven
mcp_tool_definition.description: Annual-cost comparator for an HDHP+HSA against a PPO: the break-even medical spend, the two totals at the expected spend, the winner and savings, a fixed key-spend comparison table, the HSA tax shield, and a recommendation. Pure function over the declared input domain with an explicit as_of date; the node reads no clock. Port of ApexLogics #105 (AL-112).

as_of.description: Run date, YYYY-MM-DD. Never read from a clock; echoed for determinism.

break_even_spend.description: First $50 grid point in [0, 20000] where the HDHP total is <= the PPO total; null when the HDHP is never cheaper.

input_schema_provenance: Each property is exactly the policy_parameters member the kernel reads; there is no other input surface. All fourteen properties are required; as_of is the explicit run date the port echoes in place of the Apex page wall-clock export stamp (payload DIFFERS.md S1), and the money/percent fields carry the validation bounds the kernel enforces (payload DIFFERS.md S2).
author: PostOakLabs

output_example.scope_note: Plan-cost model only: premium + in-network cost sharing to the OOP maximum, minus the HSA tax shield on contributions up to the coverage limit. No FSA/HRA interactions, no out-of-network or balance-billing, no prescription-tier carve-outs, no premium tax credits, no state-specific HSA deduction rules, and no investment growth on HSA balances. The HSA catch-up contribution for age 55+ is not applied (the source page does not apply it). Totals are the source page's own dollar arithmetic, unrounded; display rounds to cents.
